d74d33049fd71591: It can be normal. Object widths, strokes, and internal whitespace all affect perceived spacing. First confirm whether you are equalizing center distances or edge gaps, then make small optical corrections.

fce62772e9d58cb2: For repeated buttons, distinguish the button area from its internal icon. Button areas can share dimensions and spacing while the icons receive appropriate optical size adjustments. fd95f942d55064b2: Check your version's selection scope and alignment target first. Do not assume hidden or locked objects automatically participate in alignment. Explicitly set the target and observe which objects actually move.

10552d288097ec97: Check the unit beside every number, the export area, and the pixel dimensions first. Document units and export pixels serve different purposes; equal numbers do not necessarily mean equal sizes.
153e2e4fe414533e: You can prepare vector or PDF files, but confirm bleed, color requirements, font handling, and finished dimensions with the printer. This exercise does not replace print proofing or promise a particular printing color standard.
2700b59a1b8d2d78: Choose PNG in Export and Share and confirm the final dimensions and preview. A 512×512 file and a 1024×1024 file are different raster deliverables. 28c66b2070363f7d: Check pixel dimensions again during export
33b795d08585ccaf: For the square exercise, leave roughly 48 canvas units on all sides and keep the main shape in the central area. Focusing too early on tiny coordinate errors can obscure larger problems such as an oversized title or a subject too close to the edge. Near a boundary, inspect the actual contour and outer stroke edge, not only the path centerline.
5c3077a78ba8e38f: Use millimeters for a defined physical size
629399121462b2f8: Add a thick stroke near the canvas edge and check whether it is clipped. If it is, increase the composition's margins and export again.
6b945aab97afdde7: Open both images at the same displayed width and see whether their compositions match. Then inspect their file properties to distinguish displayed size from actual pixels.
6dc5a1ddd5e37c8c: Export the same original as 512×512 and 1024×1024 PNGs. Include the pixel dimensions in each filename so you can compare them without overwriting either.

8f6cb6916fb7464a: For a printed card, create a separate document 100 mm wide and 150 mm tall, then mark an inner margin of about 8 mm with a rectangle as a composition guide. Millimeters describe physical size; print clarity also depends on the file's content and the printing process. Do not equate 100 mm with 100 px. When changing units, watch whether the dimensions convert and recheck the aspect ratio rather than changing numbers while overlooking their units.
90c7bca7bbb413ac: Canvas dimensions define the document's working area; object dimensions define a shape's geometry; zoom changes only your viewing distance on screen; PNG pixel dimensions determine how many samples the exported raster image contains. Zooming in does not add image pixels. For example, a circle spanning half the canvas width occupies more screen space when zoomed in, but its proportion relative to the canvas stays unchanged.
9f7822b2679e8e6c: Understand four easily confused kinds of size
af586ca25ac442ab: Suppose you are delivering a card 100 mm wide to a workflow that accepts only images and requires a specific pixel width. Confirm the recipient's specification first, then prepare the pixel file during export. Do not simply switch canvas units from millimeters to pixels and reuse the original numbers. Physical width, image pixels, and print scaling must work together. Write the requirement as a complete sentence: “What is the finished width in millimeters, what is the delivered image width in pixels, and is scaling allowed when printing?” This is clearer than merely asking for high resolution.
b2f5ca0aa2cf1bd5: Before creating a document, note where the work will be used, whether it is landscape or portrait, and the final file type. The first exercise is a square web icon; the second is a portrait event card with room for text above and below. Both can use vector paths, but their aspect ratios differ. Stretching a square design into a rectangle turns circles into ellipses. These values are exercise suggestions, not app capacity limits or universal platform upload specifications.
b63828c0a2b21966: From the gallery, create a canvas with a purpose-specific name such as “Mountain Icon_Practice.” Open custom dimensions, choose px, enter 512 for both width and height, and verify the units and values before creating it. e8e219a72a2f91e7: Finally, inspect source images. A photo with few pixels retains that limitation even on a very large vector canvas. If you need a sharper photo, replace the source with a sufficiently detailed one rather than merely raising canvas or export numbers.
f160d9d1ce787e34: Another common issue is a mismatch between the canvas ratio and the target container. If one design must serve both a banner and a square avatar, reuse the graphic elements but arrange them separately, with clear names for both versions.
fded4f1079ccc0b4: No. Zoom helps you inspect nodes and edges; PNG quality depends on final pixels and source quality. Review the result at its normal usage size first, then zoom in to locate problems instead of editing only at extreme magnification.

18b4566317690fc2: SVG is useful when vector structure is needed
1961d283730e6749: PDF supports page delivery, but does not make everything editable
198495581904f2a4: Suppose a design contains a vector emblem, a title, and a photo. In PNG, all three become pixels together. In SVG, the emblem may retain paths, the text needs font and layout support, and the photo retains its original pixel characteristics. PDF can represent their page appearance. One vector emblem does not make every element in the whole file pure vector with unlimited detail.
1d759f0f5fa07e30: SVG can describe paths, shapes, text, and some appearance features, making it useful for further editing or rendering in compatible workflows. It can also contain bitmaps, so exporting SVG does not automatically convert photos into paths. Check object types, fonts, and complex effects before handoff. If the recipient sees only an embedded image, explain its editing limitations rather than repeatedly changing its extension.
27b5e8063db13069: Open every final format at least once in its intended environment and check shapes, text, colors, background, and dimensions. For PNG, inspect actual pixels; for SVG, editable structure and appearance; for PDF, page boundaries and readability. Return to the original to confirm that the latest changes reached the output. Export success means a file was created; completed delivery also requires that the recipient can use it correctly.
2f61d9317014ba61: Further exercise: prepare a delivery package for one icon
2fbc8c39a508ca83: Do not rely on an interchange format as your only working copy. Applications may interpret hierarchy, text, and special appearances differently. Keeping the original makes it easier to continue the current creative workflow.
3d2b61a2cb77d60d: Vector paths can be rendered again at different sizes, but photos in the document still have their original pixel limits. An SVG or PDF extension alone does not prove the entire file has no resolution constraints.
3e00997f825038a4: Record each filename, purpose, dimensions, transparency, whether text remains editable, and whether bitmaps are included. For example: “icon_512.png: web preview, transparent background”; “icon.svg: path exchange, includes one reference image”; “icon.VectorPaint: continued editing.” These descriptions help more than three similarly named files. If a file contains unused resources, clean a copy first so the recipient does not mistake reference material for final content.

864cf2f193ffef68: PNG provides a visual result at defined dimensions

a70c696276376fb9: Also check version consistency. All delivered files should come from one confirmed stage of the original: the PNG must not have a new heading while the SVG retains an old date. a9de9113a0137d2f: Ask what the recipient will do next

bb6b2125ae7d81aa: Split the discussion into three questions: does the emblem need reshaping, does the title need new wording, and is the photo only for display? For web imagery alone, a PNG at the required dimensions may be more convenient than a complex editable package.
d4578c4c7afabf12: PDF often preserves page structure and reading appearance and may contain both vectors and images. Do not promise that every PDF element remains editable like the original. Format selection does not replace a print proof, and viewers may handle effects differently.
e14ae6e6413e396f: A native editable file can preserve object organization and editing information closer to the current creative process. An original is not a magical backup guarantee: confirm that it opens and keep important copies in an independent location.
f653f669ae64c1be: For viewing alone, PNG is often the most direct option. For path editing, SVG is more useful. For page-based reading or document delivery, consider PDF. Keep the VectorPaint original for your own continued work. Choose based on the next task rather than which extension sounds more professional. Producing two or three files from one design is common, but each should have a clear purpose.
f86b1bc7e5afee18: Export a transparent PNG, an SVG, and an original. Give each a clear purpose instead of naming all of them “Final.”

03d424fdd6f525b9: They serve different purposes. No fill explicitly means the interior is not painted; a color with transparency is still a color setting. Use no fill for hollow-shape exercises to avoid unexpectedly revealing a solid interior when opacity changes later.
0bdf48bcd4ddab45: Fill supplies an object's interior color or gradient; stroke draws a line along its outline. Both can coexist, or you can retain only one. Create a 480×320 px canvas and draw three similarly sized circles in a row. This exercise needs only basic shapes and the appearance panel, with no extra images or fonts. Equal circle sizes make appearance differences easier to compare.
28c22a4c39918a29: Place the result against light and dark backgrounds, then inspect its edges and interior whitespace at the final display size. Object opacity affects the whole appearance, while color opacity can also change it. Establish a clear baseline with fully opaque colors first. A white background in an exported PNG viewer does not prove the object's fill is wrong; it may be the viewer's background. Judge actual transparency and object overlap instead.
31f5b9e122676a21: Duplicate a polyline and change only its join style, comparing protruding outer edges at sharp corners. Keep the color unchanged.

77783e31dd296154: Create three open lines of equal length with widths of 2, 4, and 8 pt. Compare them at normal display size and record the clearest option.
7d297a6935148431: Basic strokes are easier to exchange, but complex styles still need checking in the receiving software. Save the original and test the target application rather than treating a format name as a guarantee of identical appearance.

b1314e230cc5501b: If a thick line produces spikes at corners, check its join style and the angle. A very acute angle can create a pronounced projection with some joins. cc139e49363fe8c2: To standardize the strokes of three objects, first confirm that those objects are selected rather than the background or an entire group. If the shape disappears, check whether you accidentally selected no fill while also disabling the stroke. The path may still exist with no visible painting attributes.
f591cbdba03555ef: Finally, judge at normal display size. A delicate line when enlarged may become too faint when reduced, while a very thick line can consume internal whitespace.
